notes: Lead origin: inbound, self-serve signup. Early-stage SMB ecommerce SaaS building chat-based product FAQ and order-status assistant. Main pain: perceived latency for EU end-users after they signed up and started testing. Quote from product lead: "US users are fine, EU customers complain the bot takes too long — looks like timeouts in our front-end." Discovery summary: - Most traffic originates in NA (dev team) but end-customer base ~40% EU. - Integration is client-side fetch with default 30s timeout; repeated retries observed. - Current model selection: default hosted small-gen; customer mentioned trying larger models for quality, which increased response time and cost. - Primary asks: lower latency for EU, guidance on per-route timeouts, prompt-length best practices to reduce tokens, and quick checklist to tune perf without heavy infra changes. Recommended immediate actions provided to customer during call: 1) Region choice: route EU users to eu-west (or nearest region) via request-level region override in Hosted API — low friction for self-serve. 2) Timeouts: bump client-side timeout to 60s while POC runs and enable streaming to surface partial tokens early. 3) Prompt guidance: keep instruction/system messages compact, externalize long static context into embeddings + retrieval, use prefix caching for repeated system prompts and canned conversation turns; aim for <2000 prompt tokens for chat to hit <500ms typical generation for small models. 4) Model guidance: recommend latenc-optimized variants (smaller quantized models) for interactive chat; reserve larger models only for summary/batch jobs. 5) Cost tips: enable prefix caching and set token limits per response to avoid runaway costs. Follow-ups: SE Diego to share a short step-by-step POC checklist and a sample client timeout patch (PR-style) by 2025-11-20.
